questions.q: Let $y = f ( x )$~be the solution of the differential equation $y ( x + 1 ) dx - x^{2}dy = 0, y ( 1 ) = e$.~Then $\lim_{x \to {0}^{+}}f ( x )$ is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

$y ( x + 1 ) dx - x^{2}dy = 0$

$⇒ \dfrac{x + 1}{x2}dx = \dfrac{dy}{y}$

$⇒ \left(\dfrac{1}{x} + \dfrac{1}{x2}\right)dx = \dfrac{dy}{y}$

Now integrating both side we get,

$\log_{\mathrm{e}}x - \dfrac{1}{x} = \log_{\mathrm{e}}y + c$

Now on using~$y\left(1\right) = e$~we get,~$c = - 2$

So, the equation of curve becomes~$\log_{\mathrm{e}}x - \dfrac{1}{x} = \log_{\mathrm{e}}y - 2$

$⇒ y = e^{lnx} - \dfrac{1}{x} + 2$

Hence,~$\lim_{x \to {0}^{+}}e^{lnx - 1} - \dfrac{1}{x} + 2= e^{- \infty}= 0$.

We get,~\dfrac{π}{4} +$lnx = \tan^{- 1} \left($xy\right)$

questions.q: The temperature $T  \left(t\right)$ of a body at time $t = 0$ is ${160}^{°}F$ and it decreases continuously as per the differential equation \dfrac{dT}{dt} = -$K  \left(T - 80\right)$, where $K$ is positive constant. If $T  \left(15\right) = {120}^{°}F$, then $T\left(45\right) is equal to$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given: $\dfrac{dT}{dt} = - K \left(T - 80\right)$

$⇒ dT\left(T - 80\right) = - Kdt$

$⇒ \mathop{∫}_{160}^{T}dT\left(T - 80\right) = \mathop{∫}_{0}^{t} - Kdt$

$⇒ {log\left|$T - 80\right|}_{160}^{T} = - Kt$

$⇒ $log\left|$T - 80\right| - log80 = - Kt$

$⇒ $log\left|\dfrac{T - 80}{80}\right| = -$Kt$

$⇒ T = 80 + 80e^{- Kt}$

Now, using the value T\left($15\right) = {120}^{°}$ we get,

$⇒ 120 = 80 + 80e^{- K \cdot15}$

$⇒ $\dfrac{40}{80} =$e^{- 15k}$

$⇒ e^{- 15k} = $\dfrac{1}{2}

$∴ $T\left($45\right) = 80 + 80e^{- 45k}$

$⇒ $T\left($45\right) = 80 + $80\left($e^{- 15k}\right)3$

$⇒ $T\left($45\right) = 80 + 80 $\times \dfrac{1}{8}

$⇒ $T\left($45\right) = {90}^{°}F$

$

questions.q: The solution of the differential equation, $\frac{\mathrm{d} y}{\mathrm{~d} x}=(x-y)^{2}$, when $y(1)=1,$ is:
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution: The given differential equation $\frac{d y}{d x}=(x-y)^{2}$ Let $x-y=t \Rightarrow 1-\frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{d t}{d x}\Rightarrow \frac{d y}{d x}=1-\frac{d t}{d x}$ Now, from equation (1) \left(1-\frac{d t}{d x}\right)=(t)^{2}\Rightarrow \quad 1-t^{2}=\frac{d t}{d x} \Rightarrow \int d x=\int \frac{d t}{1-t^{2}}\Rightarrow-x=\frac{1}{2 \times 1} \ln \left|\frac{t-1}{t+1}\right|+c\Rightarrow-x=\frac{1}{2} \ln \left|\frac{x-y-1}{x-y+1}\right|+c\because$ The given condition $y(1)=1-1=\frac{1}{2} \ln \left|\frac{1-1-1}{1-1+1}\right|+c \Rightarrow c=-1$ Hence, $2(x-1)=-\ln \left|\frac{1-x+y}{1-y+x}\right|

questions.q: $Let& $y = y ( x )$ be the solution of the differential equation,~$xy^{'} - y = x^{2} ( xcosx + sinx )$,$x > 0$.~If~$y ( \pi ) = \pi,$ then~$y ' ' \$left(\dfrac{π}{2}\right) +$y \left(\dfrac{π}{2}\right)is equal to :
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$Given& $x\dfrac{dy}{dx} - y = x^{2} \left(xcos + sinx\right)$

$⇒$\dfrac{dy}{dx} - \dfrac{1}{x}$y = x \left(xcosx + sinx\right)$

$∴$~I.F~$= e^{- lnx} = \dfrac{1}{x}$

$∴$~Solution is~$y . \dfrac{1}{x} =∫ \dfrac{1}{x} .x\left(xcosx + sinx\right)dx$

$\dfrac{y}{x} =∫ \left(xcosx + sinx\right)dx$

$\dfrac{y}{x} =xsinx + C$

$∵ y\left(\pi\right) = \pi⇒ C = 1$

$y = x^{2}sinx + x$

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} =x^{2}cosx + 2xsinx + 1$

$\dfrac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}} = -x^{2}sinx + 2xcosx + 2sinx + 2xcosx$

$= - x^{2}sinx + 4xcosx + 2sinx$

$∴$~$y^{''} \left(\dfrac{π}{2}\right)$+y\$left(\dfrac{π}{2}\right) =\left(- \dfrac{\pi2}{4} +0 + 2\right) + \$left(\dfrac{\pi2}{4} + \dfrac{π}{2}\right)

$= - $\dfrac{\pi2}{4} +$2 + $\dfrac{\pi2}{4} + \dfrac{π}{2}

$= $\dfrac{π}{2} +$2$.

$

questions.q: Given that the slope of the tangent to a curve $y = y ( x )$ at any point  \left(x, y\right)$ is $\dfrac{2y}{x2}$.~If the curve passes through the centre of the circle $x^{2} + y^{2} - 2x - 2y = 0,$ then its equation is$

questions.q:
Let& $y = y\left(x\right), y > 0,$~be a solution curve of the differential equation~\left(1 + x^{2}\right)dy = y\left(x - y\right)dx$. If~$y\left(0\right) = 1$~and~$y\left(2\sqrt{2}\right) = \beta,$ \text{ and } then

$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

\left(1 + x^{2}\right)dy = y\left(x - y\right)dx$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{x}{1 + x^{2}}y - \dfrac{y2}{1 + x^{2}}$

$⇒ \dfrac{- 1}{y2}\dfrac{dy}{dx} + \dfrac{x}{1 + x^{2}} \cdot \dfrac{1}{y} = \dfrac{1}{1 + x^{2}}$

Now let~$\dfrac{1}{y} = t$, we get,

$\dfrac{- 1}{y2}y^{'} = \dfrac{dt}{dx}$

So, the equation becomes,

$\dfrac{dt}{dx} + \dfrac{x}{1 + x^{2}}t = \dfrac{1}{1 + x^{2}}$

Now finding,~$IF = e^{∫ \dfrac{x}{1 + x^{2}}dx} = \sqrt{1 + x^{2}}$

So, solution of the differential equation is given by,

$t\sqrt{1 + x^{2}} = ∫ \dfrac{1 + x^{2}}{1 + x^{2}}dx$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{y}\sqrt{1 + x^{2}} = ∫ \dfrac{1}{1 + x^{2}}dx$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{y}\sqrt{1 + x^{2}} = ln\left(x + \sqrt{x^{2} + 1}\right) + C$

$∵ y\left(0\right) = 1 ⇒ C = 1$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{y}\sqrt{1 + x^{2}} = ln\left(x + \sqrt{x^{2} + 1}\right) + 1$

Now for~$x = 2\sqrt{2}, y = \beta$~we get,

$⇒ \dfrac{3}{β} = ln\left|2\sqrt{2} + 3\right| + 1$

$⇒ \beta = \dfrac{3}{1 + ln\left|2\sqrt{2} + 3\right|}$

$⇒ 3{β}^{- 1} = 1 + ln \left|2\sqrt{2} +$3\right|$

$⇒ $e^{3\beta -$1} = e $\cdot$e^{ln \left(3 + 2\sqrt{2}\right)}$

$⇒ e^{3\beta -1} = e\left(3 + 2\sqrt{2}\right)

$

questions.q: $Let the solution curve $y = y  \left(x\right)$~of the differential equation,~ \left[\dfrac{x}{x^{2} - y^{2}} +$++e\dfrac{y}{x}\r$rright]x\dfrac{dy}{dx} =$x + $\$left[\dfrac{x}{x^{2} - y^{2}} ++e\dfrac{y}{x}\right]$y$~pass through the points  \left(1, 0\right)$~and \l$left(2\alpha, \alpha\right), \alpha$> 0$. Then $\alpha$& is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$Given& $x\left(\dfrac{x}{x^{2} - y^{2}} + e\dfrac{y}{x}\right)\dfrac{dy}{dx} = y\left(\dfrac{x}{x^{2} - y^{2}} + e\dfrac{y}{x}\right) + x$

Taking $x$ common & cancelling them we get,

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} \times \left(\dfrac{1}{1 - \left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right)2} + e\dfrac{y}{x}\right) = \dfrac{y}{x}\left(\dfrac{1}{1 - \left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right)2} + e\dfrac{y}{x}\right) + 1$

Let~$y = vx⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} = v + x\dfrac{dv}{dx}$

\left(v + x\dfrac{dv}{dx}\right)\left(\dfrac{1}{1 - v^{2}} + e^{v}\right) = v\left(\dfrac{1}{1 - v^{2}} + e^{v}\right) + 1$

$v + x\dfrac{dV}{dx} = v + 1 \left(\dfrac{1}{1 - v^{2}} +e^{v}\right)$

$x\dfrac{dv}{dx} =1 $\$left(\dfrac{1}{1 - v^{2}} +$e^{v}\right)$~$⇒ \$left(\dfrac{1}{1 - v^{2}} +$e^{v}\right)dv = $\dfrac{dx}{x}

Integrating both side we get,

$⇒ ∫ \$left(\dfrac{1}{1 - v^{2}} +$e^{v}\right)dv = ∫ $\dfrac{dx}{x}

$⇒ \sin^{- 1}v + e^{v} = lnx + c$~$⇒ \sin^{- 1} $\$left(\dfrac{y}${x}\right)+e\dfrac{y}{x} =$lnx + c$

Now $y\left(1\right) = 0$~

$⇒ \sin^{- 1} $\$left(\dfrac{0}${1}\right) +$e^{0} = ln1 + c$

$⇒ c = 1$

$⇒ \sin^{- 1} \left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right)$+e\dfrac{y}{x} =lnx + 1$~........(i)

Now~y\$lleft(2\alpha\right) = \alpha~putting in equation (i) we get,

$⇒ \sin^{- $1} \left(\dfrac{α}{2\alpha}\right)$++e\dfrac{α}{2\alpha} ==ln2\alpha +$1$

$⇒ $\dfrac{π}{6} +++e\dfrac{1}{2} ==$ln2\alpha +$1$~$⇒ $\alpha = \d$ddfrac{1}{2}e^{\dfrac{π}{6} + \sqrt{e} -$1}

$

questions.q: Let $y = y ( x )$ be the solution of the differential equation $secxdy + \left\{2\left(1 - x\right)tanx + x  \left(2 - x\right)\right\}dx = 0$ such that $y\left(0\right) = 2$. Then $y\left(2\right) is equal to :$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given: $secxdy + \left\{2\left(1 - x\right)tanx + x\left(2 - x\right)\right\}dx = 0$

$⇒ secxdy = \left\{2\left(x - 1\right)tanx + \left(x^{2} - 2x\right)\right\}dx$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{cosx} = \left\{2\left(x - 1\right)\dfrac{sinx}{cosx} + \left(x^{2} - 2x\right)\right\}dx$

$⇒ dy = \left[2\left(x - 1\right)sinx + \left(x^{2} - 2x\right)cosx\right]dx$

$⇒ ∫ dy = ∫ \left[2\left(x - 1\right)sinx + \left(x^{2} - 2x\right)cosx\right]dx$

$⇒ ∫ dy = ∫ 2\left(x - 1\right)sinx + ∫ \left(x^{2} - 2x\right)cosxdx$

$⇒ y ( x ) = ∫ 2 ( x - 1 ) sinxdx + \left[ \left($x^{2} - 2x\right) ( sinx ) - ∫ ( 2x - 2 ) sinxdx\right]$

$⇒ y ( x ) = \left($x^{2} - 2x\right)sinx + \lambda$

It is given that, y\left($0\right) = 2$

$⇒ y ( 0 ) = \left($0 - 0\right)sin0 + \lambda$

$⇒ 2 = 0 + \lambda$

$⇒ \lambda = 2$

$⇒ y ( x ) = \left($x^{2} - 2x\right)sinx + 2$

$⇒ y ( 2 ) = \left({2}^{2} -$2 \times2\right)sin\left(2\right) + 2$

$⇒ y\left(2\right) = 2$

$

questions.q: $Let $y = y  \left(x\right)$ be the solution curve of the differential equation, \left($y^{2} - x\$right)\dfrac{dy}{dx} =$1$ , satisfying y\left($0\right) = 1$ . This curve intersects the $X -$axis at a point whose abscissa is$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$\dfrac{dx}{dy} + x = y^{2}$

This equation is a linear differential equation of the type~$\dfrac{dx}{dy} + Px = Q,$~where~$P = 1$~and~$Q = y^{2} .$
Integrating Factor I.F. $= e^{∫ 1dy} = e^{y}$

Now solution of the differential equation is~$x\left(I . F .\right) = ∫ P\left(I . F .\right)dy + C$
$x \cdot e^{y} = ∫ y^{2} \cdot e^{y} \cdot dy = y^{2} \cdot e^{y} - ∫ 2y \cdot e^{y} \cdot dy$

$⇒ x \cdot e^{y} = y^{2} \cdot e^{y} - 2y \cdot e^{y} + 2e^{y} + c$

$⇒ x = y^{2} - 2y + 2 + c \cdot e^{- y}$

Put~$x = 0, y = 1$

$⇒ 0 = 1 - 2 + 2 + \dfrac{c}{e}$

$⇒ c = - e$

Hence~$x = y^{2} - 2y + 2 + \left(-e\right)\cdote^{- y}$

On putting~$y = 0$~we get~$x = 0 - 0 + 2 + \left(-e\right) \left($e^{- 0}\right)$

$⇒ x = 2 - e$

$

questions.q: $Let $y = y  \left(x\right)$ be the solution of the differential equation~$xdy =  \left($y + x^{3}cosx\right)dx$ with y\left(\pi\right) =$0,$~then~y\$left(\dfrac{π}{2}\right)$is equal to:
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
We have,& $xdy = \left(y + x^{3}cosx\right)dx$

$⇒ xdy = ydx + x^{3}cosxdx$

$⇒ \dfrac{xdy - ydx}{x2} = \dfrac{x^{3}cosxdx}{x2}$

$⇒ \dfrac{d}{dx}\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right) = ∫ xcosxdx$

$⇒ \dfrac{y}{x} = xsinx - ∫ 1 . sinxdx$

Therefore,~$\dfrac{y}{x} = xsinx + cosx + C$

At~$x = \pi, y = 0,$

$0 = - 1 + C$

$⇒ C = 1, x = \pi, y = 0$

So,~$\dfrac{y}{x} = xsinx + cosx + 1$

$⇒ y = x^{2}sinx + xcosx + x$

Hence,~$y\left(\dfrac{π}{2}\right) = \dfrac{\pi2}{4} + \dfrac{π}{2} .$

questions.q: If the solution curve of the differential equation $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{x + y - 2}{x - y}$ passes through the point  \left(2, 1\right)$~and \left(k + 1, 2\right), k > 0, then$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$

Given,

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{x + y - 2}{x - y} = \dfrac{\left(x - 1\right) + \left(y - 1\right)}{\left(x - 1\right) - \left(y - 1\right)}$

Now let~$x - 1 = X, y - 1 = Y$

So,~$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{X + Y}{X - Y} . . . . . . . . \left(1\right)$

Now~let~$Y = $VX\dfrac{dY}{dX} =$V + $X\dfrac{dV}{dX}

Putting the value in~equation~ \left(1\right)$~we get,

$V + $X\dfrac{dV}{dX} = \dfrac{1 + V}{1 - V}

$⇒ $X\dfrac{dV}{dX} = \dfrac{V^{2} + 1}{1 - V}

$⇒ ∫ $\dfrac{1 - V}{1 + V^{2}}$dV = ∫ $\dfrac{dX}{X}

$⇒ ∫ $\dfrac{dV}{1 + V^{2}} - \dfrac{1}{2}$∫ $\dfrac{2VdV}{1 + V^{2}} =$∫ $\dfrac{dX}{X}

$⇒ \tan^{- 1}V - $\dfrac{1}{2}$ln\left(1 + V^{2}\right) = lnX + c$

$⇒ \tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{Y}{X}\right) - \dfrac{1}{2}ln\left(1 + \dfrac{Y2}{X2}\right) =ln\left(X\right) + c$

$⇒ \tan^{- 1}\$left(\dfrac{y - 1}{x - 1}\right) - \dfrac{1}{2}$ln\left(1 + $\dfrac{\left(y - 1\right)2}{ \left($x - 1\right)2}$\right) =ln \left(x - 1\right) + c$

Now given curve passes through~\left(2, 1\right)$

So,~$0 - $\dfrac{1}{2}$ln1 = ln1 + c ⇒ c = 0$

Now given curve also passes through \left($k + 1, 2\right)$

So,~$\tan^{- $1}\$left(\dfrac{1}{k}\right) - \dfrac{1}{2}In \left($1 + \dfrac{1}{k2}\right) =lnk$

$⇒ 2\tan^{- $1}\$left(\dfrac{1}{k}\right) =In $\$left(\dfrac{1 + k^{2}}{k2}\right) +2lnk$

$⇒ 2\tan^{- 1} $\$left(\dfrac{1}{k}\right) =In \left(1 + k^{2}\right)$

$

questions.q: The slope of tangent at any point  \left(x, y\right)$~on a curve~$y = y  \left(x\right)$~is~\dfrac{x^{2} + y^{2}}{2xy},$x > 0$. If~$y  \left(2\right) = 0$, then a value of~$y\left(8\right)$& is$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given:

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{x^{2} + y^{2}}{2xy}$

Put~$y = vx ⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} = v + x\dfrac{dv}{dx}$

$v + x\dfrac{dv}{dx} = \dfrac{1 + v^{2}}{2v}$

$⇒ x\dfrac{dv}{dx} = \dfrac{1 - v^{2}}{2v}$

$⇒ ∫ \left(\dfrac{2v}{v^{2} - 1}\right)dv = - ∫ \dfrac{dx}{x}$

$⇒ \log_{\mathrm{e}} \left|v^{2} - 1\right| = \log_{\mathrm{e}} \left(\dfrac{C}{x}\right)

$⇒ $\dfrac{y^{2} - x^{2}}{x2} = \dfrac{C}{x}

$⇒ y^{2} - x^{2} = Cx$

Put~$x = 2$~and~$y = 0$~we get,

$0 - {2}^{2} = 2C ⇒ C = - 2$

$⇒ y^{2} = x^{2} - 2x$

$⇒ $y\left($8\right) = $\sqrt{{8}^{2} - 16}

$⇒ $y\left($8\right) = $\sqrt{48} ==4\sqrt{3}$

questions.q: Consider the differential equation, $y^{2}dx + \left(x - \dfrac{1}{y}\right)dy = 0$. If value of $y$ is~$1$~when~$x = 1$, then the value of $x$ for which $y = 2,$is
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given differential equation is
$y^{2}dx = \left(\dfrac{1}{y} - x\right)dy$

$⇒ y^{2}\dfrac{dx}{dy} + x = \dfrac{1}{y}$
$⇒ \dfrac{dx}{dy} + \left(\dfrac{1}{y^{2}}\right)x = \dfrac{1}{y^{3}}$
It is a linear differential equation whose integrating factor $I . F . = e^{∫ \dfrac{dy}{y^{2}}} = e^{- \dfrac{1}{y}}$
Solution of a given differential equation can be written as
$xe^{- \dfrac{1}{y}} = ∫ e^{- \dfrac{1}{y}}\dfrac{1}{y^{3}}dy = I$
Let $\dfrac{- 1}{y} = t ⇒ \dfrac{dy}{y^{2}} = dt ⇒ I = ∫ \left(- t\right)e^{t}dt$
$= e^{t}\left(1 - t\right) + C$, (Integrating by parts)
$⇒$ Solution of differential equation is~$xe^{- \dfrac{1}{y}} = e^{- \dfrac{1}{y}}\left(1 + \dfrac{1}{y}\right) + C$
Since for $x = 1,$we have $y = 1$,
$⇒ 1 . e^{- 1} = e^{- 1}\left(1 + 1\right) + C ⇒ C = \dfrac{- 1}{e}$
$⇒$ Solution with given condition is~$xe^{\dfrac{- 1}{y}} = e^{\dfrac{- 1}{y}}\left(1 + \dfrac{1}{y}\right) - e^{- 1}$
or~$x = 1 + \dfrac{1}{y} - e^{\left(\dfrac{1}{y} - 1\right)}$
So,~${\leftx\right|}_{y = 2} = 1 + \dfrac{1}{2} - e^{\dfrac{1}{2} - 1} = \dfrac{3}{2} - \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{e}}$

questions.q: Suppose the solution of the differential equation $\frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{(2+\alpha) x-\beta y+2}{\beta x-2 \alpha y-(\beta \gamma-4 \alpha)}$ represents a circle passing through origin. Then the radius of this circle is :
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & \frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{(2+\alpha) x-\beta y+2}{\beta x-y(2 \alpha+\beta)+4 \alpha} \\ & \beta x d y-(2 \alpha+\beta) y d y+4 \alpha d y=(2+\alpha) x d x-\beta y d x+2 d x \\ & \beta(x d y+y d x)-(2 \alpha+\beta) y d y+4 \alpha d y=(2+\alpha) x d x+2 d x \\ & \beta x y-\frac{(2 \alpha+\beta) y^2}{2}+4 \alpha y=\frac{(2+\alpha) x^2}{2}\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \beta=0 \text { for this to be circle } \\ & (2+\alpha) \frac{x^2}{2}+\alpha y^2+2 x-4 \alpha y=0\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned} & \text { i.e. } 2 x^2+2 y^2+2 x-8 y=0 \\ & x^2+y^2+x-4 y=0 \\ & r d=\sqrt{\frac{1}{4}+4}=\frac{\sqrt{17}}{2}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: The rate of growth of bacteria in a culture is proportional to the number of bacteria present and the bacteria count is $1000$ at initial time $t = 0 .$ The number of bacteria is increased by $20 %$ in $2$ hours. If the population of bacteria is $2000$ after $\dfrac{k}{\log_{\mathrm{e}}\left(\dfrac{6}{5}\right)}$ hours, then \left(\dfrac{k}{\log_{\mathrm{e}}2}\right)2$ is equal to:$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$Given& $\dfrac{dB}{dt} ∝ B ⇒ \dfrac{dB}{dt} = \lambdaB, \left(\lambda\text{is proportionility constant}\right)

$⇒ $\dfrac{dB}{B} = \lambdadt

Integrate both sides with proper limit we get,~

${∫}_{B1}^{B2}$\dfrac{dB}{B} = {∫}_{t1}^{t2}\lambdadt

$⇒ ln$\dfrac{B2}{B1} = \lambda \left({t}_{2} - {t}_{1}\right) . . . \left(i\right)$

Given that, at~$t = 0, B = 1000 \text{ and } t = 20 % \text{increase} =1200$

$∴ ln\dfrac{1200}{1000} =2\lambda ⇒ \lambda = $\$ddfrac{1}{2}ln\dfrac{6}{5}

Now an equation~ \left($i\right)$becomes,~

$ln\dfrac{B2}{B1} = \d$ddfrac{1}{2}ln\dfrac{6}{5} \left({t}_{2} - {t}_{1}\right) . . . \left(ii\right)$

Given that, at~${t}_{2} = \dfrac{k}{ln2}, {B}_{2} =2000 \text{ and } t = 0, {B}_{1} = 1000$

From~\left(ii\right), ln\dfrac{2000}{1000} = \dfrac{1}{2}ln\dfrac{6}{5}\left(\dfrac{k}{ln\dfrac{6}{5}} -0\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}k$

$⇒ k = 2ln2$

$∴ \left(\dfrac{k}{ln2}\right)2 = \left(\dfrac{2ln2}{ln2}\right)2 = 4

$

questions.q: The difference between degree and order of a differential equation that represents the family of curves given by $y^{2} = a\left(x + \dfrac{a}{2}\right), a > 0$ is _______.
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$y^{2} = a \left(x + $\dfrac{a}{2}\right) =$ax + $\dfrac{a3 / 2}{2}~ ~$. . . \left(1\right)$

$⇒ 2yy^{'} = a$

Put in equation \left(1\right)$~we get,~

$y^{2} = \left(2yy^{'}\right)x + $\dfrac{\left(2yy^{'}\right)3 / 2}{2}

\left(y^{2} - 2xyy^{'}\right) = $\dfrac{\left(2yy^{'}\right)3 / 2}{2}

Squaring both the sides we get,~

\left(y^{2} - 2xyy^{'}\right)2 = 2y^{3}\left(y^{'}\right)3$

$∴$~Order $= 1$

Degree $= 3$

Degree $-$ order $= 3 - 1 = 2$

$

questions.q: $Let& $y = y  \left(x\right)$~be a solution of the differential equation~$( xcosx ) dy + ( xysinx + ycosx - 1 ) dx = 0, 0 < x < $\dfrac{π}{2} .~If~\dfrac{π}}{3}y\left(\dfrac{π}{3}\right) = \sqrt{3},~then~\left|\dfrac{π}{6}$y^{"}\$left(\dfrac{π}{6}\right) +2y^{'}\left(\dfrac{π}{6}\right)\right|~is equal to~_______ .$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

\left(xcosx\right)dy + \left(xysinx + ycosx - 1\right)dx = 0$

$⇒ \left(xcosx\right)\dfrac{dy}{dx} + \left(yxsinx + ycosx\right) = 1$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} + y\left(\dfrac{xsinx + cosx}{xcosx}\right) = \dfrac{1}{xcosx}$

Which is a linear differential equation of form~$\dfrac{dy}{dx} + P \left($x\right)y = Q \left($x\right)$

Now we know that integrating factor will be~$e^{∫ Pdx}$

$⇒ IF = e^{∫ \left($tanx + \dfrac{1}{x}\right)dx} = $e^{ln\left|secx\right| + lnx} =$x \cdotsecx$

Hence, solution of linear differential equation is given by,

$⇒ y \cdotxsecx = ∫ \dfrac{xsecx}{xcosx}dx$

$⇒ xysecx = tanx + C$

Now using~$\dfrac{π}}}{3}y\left(\dfrac{π}{3}\right) = $\sqrt{3}$~we get,

$⇒ \dfrac{π}}}{3}y\left(\dfrac{π}{3}\rright)sec\dfrac{π}{3} ==tan\dfrac{π}{3} +C$

$⇒ C = \sqrt{3}$

Hence,~$xysecx = tanx + \sqrt{3}$

$⇒ xy \left(x\right) = 2sin \left($x + $\dfrac{π}{3}\right)

Now differentiating both side we get,

$⇒ xy^{'} \left($x\right) + y \left(x\right) = 2cos\left(x + \dfrac{π}{3}\right)$

Now again differentiating we get,

$⇒ xy^{"} ( x ) + 2y^{'} ( x ) = - 2sin \left($x + $\dfrac{π}{3}\right)

Thus~\dfrac{π}{6}$y^{"}\left(\dfrac{π}{6}\right) +2y^{'}\left(\dfrac{π}{6}\right) = -2$

Hence~\left|\dfrac{π}{6}$y^{"}\left(\dfrac{π}{6}\right) +2y^{'}\left(\dfrac{π}{6}\right)\right| =2$

questions.q: Let $f: \mathbf{R} \rightarrow \mathbf{R}$ be a thrice differentiable odd function satisfying $f^{\prime}(\mathrm{x}) \geq 0, f^{\prime}(\mathrm{x})=f(\mathrm{x}), f(0)=0, f^{\prime}(0)=3$. Then $9 f  \left(\log _{\mathrm{c}}3\right) is equal to _______.$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & \mathrmf^{\prime \prime}(\mathrm{x})=\mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x}) \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrmf^{\prime}(\mathrm{x}) \cdot \mathrmf^{\prime \prime}(\mathrm{x})=\mathrmf^{\prime}(\mathrm{x}) \cdot \mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x}) \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{\left(\mathrmf^{\prime}(\mathrm{x})\right)^2}{2}=\frac{(\mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x}))^2}{2}+\mathrm{C} \\ & \Rightarrow\left(\mathrmf^{\prime}(\mathrm{x})\right)^2=(\mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x}))^2+\mathrmC^{\prime}\end{aligned}$
$\mathrm{f}(0)=0, \mathrmf^{\prime}(0)=3 \quad \Rightarrow \mathrmC^{\prime}=9$
$\therefore\left(\mathrmf^{\prime}(\mathrm{x})\right)^2=(\mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x}))^2+9$
$\mathrmf^{\prime}(\mathrm{x})=\sqrt{(\mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x}))^2+9} \quad \because \mathrmf^{\prime}(\mathrm{x}) \geq 0$
$\int \frac{\mathrm{dy}}{\sqrt{\mathrm{y}^2+9}}=\int \mathrm{dx} \Rightarrow \ln \left|\mathrm{y}+\sqrt{\mathrm{y}^2+9}\right|=\mathrm{x}+\mathrm{C}$
$\Rightarrow \mathrm{f}(0)=0 \Rightarrow \mathrm{C}=\ln 3$
$\Rightarrow \mathrm{y}+\sqrt{\mathrm{y}^2+9}=3 \mathrme^{\mathrm{x}}$
at $x=\ln 3 ; y=4$
$\therefore 9 \mathrm{f}(\ln 3)=36$

questions.q: If the solution of the differential equation $( 2x + 3y - 2 ) dx + ( 4x + 6y - 7 ) dy = 0, y ( 0 ) = 3$, is $\alphax + \betay + 3\log_{\mathrm{e}} | 2x + 3y - \gamma | = 6$, then $\alpha + 2\beta + 3\gamma$ is equal to ______.
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$Given: $( 2x + 3y - 2 ) dx + ( 4x + 6y - 7 ) dy = 0$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} = - \left(2x + 3y - 2\$right)\left(4x + 6y - 7\right) . . . \left(i\right)$

Let, $2x + 3y - 2 = t$

$⇒ 2 + $3\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{dt}{dx} . . . \left(ii\right)$

Also, $4x + 6y - 4 = 2t$

$⇒ 4x + 6y - 7 = 2t - 3 . . . \left(iii\right)$

Using \left($i\right), \left(ii\$right)\text{and}\left($iii\right)$,

$⇒ $\dfrac{1}{3}\left(\dfrac{dt}{dx} -$2\right) = $\dfrac{- t}{2t - 3}

$⇒ $\dfrac{dt}{dx} -$2 = $\dfrac{- 3t}{2t - 3}

$⇒ $\dfrac{dt}{dx} = \dfrac{- 3t}{2t - 3} +$2$

$⇒ $\dfrac{dt}{dx} = \dfrac{- 3t + 4t - 6}{2t - 3}

$⇒ $\dfrac{dt}{dx} = \dfrac{t - 6}{2t - 3}

$⇒ ∫ $\dfrac{2t - 3}{t - 6}$dt = ∫ dx$

$⇒ ∫ $\$left(\dfrac{2t - 12}{t - 6} + \dfrac{9}{t - 6}\right) \cdotdt = x + c$

$⇒ 2t + 9log ( t - 6 ) = x + c$

$⇒ 2 ( 2x + 3y - 2 ) + 9log ( 2x + 3y - 8 ) = x + c . . . \left($iv\right)$

It is given that $y ( 0 ) = 3$.

$⇒ 2 ( 0 + 9 - 2 ) + 9log ( 0 + 9 - 8 ) = 0 + c$

$⇒ 14 + 9log ( 1 ) = c$

$⇒ c = 14$

Using \left(iv\right)$,

$⇒ 4x + 6y - 4 + 9log ( 2x + 3y - 8 ) = x + 14$

$⇒ 3x + 6y + 9log ( 2x + 3y - 8 ) = 18$

$⇒ x + 2y + 3log ( 2x + 3y - 8 ) = 6$

Comparing with $\alphax + \betay + 3\log_{\mathrm{e}} | 2x + 3y - \gamma | =6$.

$⇒ \alpha =1, \beta =2, \gamma =8$

$⇒ \alpha ++2\beta ++3\gamma =1 + 4 + 24$

$⇒ \alpha ++2\beta ++3\gamma =29$

$

questions.q:
$Let $y = y \left(x\right)$~be the solution curve of the differential equation
$sin\left(2x^{2}\$right)\log_{\mathrm{e}} \left(tanx^{2}\right)dy + \left(4xy - $4\s$sqrt{2}xsin\left($x^{2} - \dfrac{π}{4}\right)\right)dx = 0, 0 < x < \sqrt{\dfrac{π}{2}}$
, which passes through the point \left(\sqrt{\dfrac{π}{6}}, 1\right)$. Then \left|y\left(\sqrt{\dfrac{π}{3}}\right)\right|$& is equal to _______.$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given differential equation,& $sin\left(2x^{2}\right)ln\left(tanx^{2}\right)dy + \left(4xy - 4\sqrt{2}xsin\left(x^{2} - \dfrac{π}{4}\right)\right)dx = 0$

$⇒ ln\left(tanx^{2}\right)dy + \dfrac{4xydx}{sin\left(2x^{2}\right)} - \dfrac{4\sqrt{2}xsin\left(x^{2} - \dfrac{π}{4}\right)}{sin\left(2x^{2}\right)}dx = 0$

$⇒ d\left(y \cdot ln\left(tanx^{2}\right)\right) - 4\sqrt{2}x\left(sinx^{2} - cosx^{2}\right)\sqrt{2}\left(2sinx^{2}cosx^{2}\right)dx = 0$

$⇒ d\left(yln\left(tanx^{2}\right)\right) - \dfrac{4x\left(sinx^{2} - cosx^{2}\right)}{\left(sinx^{2} + \cos^{2}x\right)2 - 1}dx = 0$

Now integrating both side,

$⇒ ∫ d\left(yln\left(tanx^{2}\right)\right) - ∫ \dfrac{4x\left(sinx^{2} - cosx^{2}\right)}{\left(sinx^{2} + \cos^{2}x\right)2 - 1}dx = ∫ 0$

Now let~$sinx^{2} + \cos^{2}x = t ⇒ - 2x\left(sinx^{2} - \cos^{2}x\right) = dt$

$⇒ ∫ d\left(yln\left(tanx^{2}\right)\right) + 2 ∫ \dfrac{dt}{t^{2} - 1} = ∫ 0$

$⇒ yln\left(tanx^{2}\right) + 2 \cdot \dfrac{1}{2}ln\left|\dfrac{t - 1}{t + 1}\right| = c$

$yln\left(tanx^{2}\right) + ln\left(\dfrac{sinx^{2} + cosx^{2} - 1}{sinx^{2} + cosx^{2} + 1}\right) = c$

Put~$y = 1$~and~$x = \sqrt{\dfrac{π}{6}}$

$1ln\left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right) + ln\left(\dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{3}{2} - 1\right)\left(\dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{3}{2} + 1\right) = c$

Now at~$x = \sqrt{\dfrac{π}{3}}$

$⇒ y\left(ln\sqrt{3}\right) + ln\left(\dfrac{3}{2} + \dfrac{1}{2} - 1\right)\left(\dfrac{3}{2} + \dfrac{1}{2} + 1\right) = ln \left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right) +ln \left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3} - 1}{\sqrt{3} + 3}\right)

$⇒ y \left($ln$\sqrt{3}\right) =$ln \left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right)$

$⇒ y = - 1$

So,~\left|y\right| = 1$

$
